title: Production Evals For Agentic AI Systems - Nishant Gupta, Meta Superintelligence Labs
talk_summary: The talk argues agentic evals must shift from model benchmarks to production system behavior: scenario-based offline evals, execution traces, continuous monitoring, and targeted human review. It recommends SRE-style metrics like task completion, tool success, escalation, latency, cost, and recovery, with evaluation treated as a control-plane service.

takeaways.what_they_do: They evaluate realistic workflows/scenarios rather than isolated prompts, measuring task completion, tool correctness, planning quality, and resource usage inside a simulated environment.
takeaways.evidence_quote: agent evaluation should be scenario driven, not prompt driven

takeaways.what_they_do: They collect execution traces, user outcomes, escalations, failures, and feedback so real production interactions become the largest evaluation dataset.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Production traffic is no longer just traffic. It becomes evaluation data.

takeaways.what_they_do: They treat evaluation as an always-running service that detects slow degradation after model, prompt, tool, or user-behavior changes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: evaluation is an always-running service, not a testing phase

takeaways.what_they_do: They map agent metrics to business outcomes: task completion, tool success, escalation rate, safety violations, latency, cost, and recovery rate, explicitly not just accuracy.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Task completion measures value delivered. Tool success measures operational reliability. Escalation rate measures human burden.

takeaways.technique: Targeted human review as evaluator calibration
takeaways.what_they_do: They use humans not as fallback but as evaluators who assess correctness, trust, usefulness, and safety, then feed those signals back to calibrate automated metrics.
They separate the execution plane that does work from a control plane that observes telemetry, runs simulations, coordinates human review, and governs behavior.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Evaluation becomes part of the control plane, not a separate tool
